title: Measuring Research Progress and Linguistic Inclusion in Low-Resource Languages
abstract: arXiv:2610.30296v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have accelerated research on low-resource and multilingual NLP, but their effectiveness in creating an equitable landscape remains unmapped. We analyze 1,158 peer-reviewed open-access papers published between 2020 and 2025, examining research attention to low-resource languages (LRLs) and representation across language and speaker populations. To assess linguistic inclusion beyond publication counts, we introduce the Linguistic Inclusion Framework (LIF), a multidimensional framework that measures linguistic inclusion in four dimensions: research growth, representation expansion, representation continuity, and distributional equity. While annual publications grew from 52 to 415, a 5.4X increase in their ACL Anthology publication share, this growth largely concentrated on represented languages rather than expanding coverage of underrepresented languages. translated_title: 衡量低资源语言的研究进展与语言包容性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）加速了低资源与多语言自然语言处理（NLP）的研究，但它们在构建公平研究格局方面的有效性仍不明朗。我们分析了2020年至2025年间发表的1,158篇同行评审开放获取论文，考察了对低资源语言（LRLs）的研究关注度及其在语言和语言使用者群体中的代表性。为了超越单纯的论文发表数量来评估语言包容性，我们引入了语言包容性框架（LIF），这是一个从四个维度衡量语言包容性的多维框架：研究增长、代表性扩展、代表性延续性和分布公平性。尽管年度发表论文数量从52篇增长到415篇，在ACL Anthology的论文份额中增长了5.4倍，但这种增长主要集中于已被代表的语言，而非扩展对代表性不足语言的覆盖。进一步分析显示，亚洲使用的语言占据……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出语言包容性框架（LIF），通过分析2020-2025年间1,158篇论文发现，尽管低资源语言NLP研究论文数量增长了5.4倍，但增长主要集中于已被代表的主流语言，而非真正扩展对代表性不足语言的覆盖。
